source: NASA/JPL Mars 2020 public traverse (mars.nasa.gov MMGIS layers)
finding: The first version of our map treated ridge, rim and delta-front lines as impassable, but 12.0% of the real drive path lay on them, all on slopes under 20 degrees. Validation caught this; they are now high-cost caution ground, and the map was re-checked.
caveats: The rover has different mobility limits than an astronaut on foot.
The drives were chosen by JPL planners, so agreement shows consistency with real drive planning, not proof of crew safety.
Our grid is 75 m; rover localisation and the elevation model have their own errors.
